label: TSMM to OASF binding
description: Maps Open Agentic Schema Framework (OASF) publication and evaluation structures into TSMM abstractions so OASF-described agents become assurance-addressable without collapsing TSMM into a schema catalog.

mappings.description: Published machine-readable description of an agent or service surface that can be evaluated as a trust-relevant service description.
Entity accountable for publishing and maintaining the described agent or service record.
Composable extension point used to attach bounded semantics, assurance metadata, or ecosystem-specific publication requirements.
Structured interaction metadata describing communication surface, protocol attachment, and operational context relevant to trust decisions.
Structured evaluation output describing observed results, scores, and findings over a subject or artifact.
Reference to an externally produced evaluation artifact that can be cited as evidence in later assurance decisions.

notes: The binding is intentionally lightweight. It lets TSMM point to OASF-described subjects and evaluation artifacts without turning OASF into a trust semantics replacement.
Assurance-addressable means TSMM entities can be referenced by OASF-aware control catalogs, evidence bundles, and evaluation outputs.

guarantees.name: publication-and-evaluation-addressability
guarantees.description: OASF publication and evaluation artifacts can be associated with TSMM service, accountability, assessment, and evidence semantics.

limitations.name: publication-enforcement-gap
limitations.impact: A published OASF record or evaluation reference does not establish runtime authorization, control effectiveness, or revocation processing.
limitations.mitigation: Pair publication artifacts with authority, policy, evidence, decision, and status records appropriate to the effect being considered.

behavioralExpectations.expectation: A TSMM-aware OASF publication SHOULD identify the accountable operator, applicable policy or profile, and evidence or evaluation references.

notes: Suitable for bounded publication and evaluation comparison; runtime governance must be composed separately.
